newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cordoba could push up Argentine jobless rate-paper.
newsitem.headline: Cordoba could push up Argentine jobless rate-paper.

text.p: A rise in unemployment in Argentina's second biggest city, Cordoba, means the national unemployment rate may have to be revised upwards to 17.6 percent from 17.3 percent, La Nacion newspaper said Wednesday.
The latest release of Argentina's twice-yearly jobless data, measured in October and announced in December, did not include Cordoba because of logistical problems.
But the paper quoted the delayed survey of Greater Cordoba showing unemployment of 18.6 percent by October versus 17.2 percent in May and 15.9 percent in October 1995.
The national data released last month assumed a jobless rate in Cordoba in line with the average of cities in the interior of the country of 15 percent.

If the National Statistics Institute considers the new data valid it will have to raise the national jobless rate -- which compares with 17.1 percent in May 1996, 16.4 percent in October 1995 and a record 18.4 percent in May 1995.

But one Statistics Institute official told Reuters that at the time of the jobless survey in Cordoba, civil servants were on strike, which delayed the survey and could affect the accuracy of the data.

Normally households are polled on what their employment status was the week prior to the survey. But in Cordoba, there was a gap of two or three weeks between the week of reference and the survey itself, which could make data less reliable, the official said.
